IBM.rationale: IBM presents a mildly-to-moderately attractive fundamental picture. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): YoY trends are solid — Q1 2026 revenue +9.5%, EPS +14.3%, OCF +18.3%, gross margin +100bps, operating margin +70bps — but extreme QoQ volatility (EPS -44.6% QoQ) and the ambiguity over whether Q1 2026 standalone margins (~7.7% net) or trailing blended margins (~15.6% net) are representative of the run rate temper conviction. Debt-to-equity of 3.73x is elevated. The franchise is genuine: Red Hat OpenShift, >$12B cumulative watsonx bookings, mainframe switching costs, and 95% Fortune 500 penetration. Pillar 2 (valuation): P/E has compressed from 46x to 26.7x over the past year while ROE expanded from 20.3% to 32.5% — the market is paying less for better profitability. P/E sits in the lower third of its 19–51x range. However, if Q1 2026 margins are the true run rate, the 'real' P/E could be 40–50x, undermining the cheapness thesis. P/B at 8.7x is mid-range. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The CHIPS Act $1B quantum funding, $10B quantum investment commitment, Google Cloud partnership, and Project Lightwell are all catalyst-dense, but the stock already rallied ~20% on these headlines and then gave back 7.9% in a single day (2026-06-03) with RSI at 85.47, suggesting the near-term catalysts are largely priced in. The quantum and partnership items are multi-year with negligible near-term P&L impact. Net: positive trajectory and improved valuation support a mild positive tilt, but earnings quality ambiguity, leverage, and catalyst exhaustion after the recent run keep the score moderate.
